newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean fruit exports rise 13 pct 95/96 season.
newsitem.headline: Chilean fruit exports rise 13 pct 95/96 season.

text.p: Chile's fruit exports rose to $1.2 billion in the 1995/1996 season, up 13 percent on the previous season, said the Chilean Exporters Association.
"It has been a good season, although we have had some serious one-off problems," said president Ronald Bown.
"Each species has to be analyzed individually, but in general terms we had good volume and good prices."
In volume, exports totalled 167 million cases, up eight percent from the 1994/1995 period, said the association.
Main markets included the United States, which received 36 percent of total exports, followed by Europe with 35 percent and Latin America at 19 percent.
Top growth was seen in exports of pears, grapes, plums and kiwi fruit with peaches the only species in which exports fell last season.
